newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ends near new peaks as cyclicals rally.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends near new peaks as cyclicals rally.

text.p: Shares hit records on Tuesday following a strong rally on Wall Street overnight, but ended a shade below intra-session peaks as Nokia inched lower at the open in New York, dimming the outlook slightly, brokers said.

The HEX general index rose over one percent in early trade and stayed comfortably above the psychologically important 3,000 point level. It closed up 1.12 percent at a 3,031.04 record close, having set a new 3,041.92 all-time high earlier.
The FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark also set a new record at 1,057.68, but closed a shade lower at 1,052.93, still up a strong 1.14 percent.
"The U.S. open suggests a (downward) correction tommorrow," one broker said.
Nokia closed at its session low -- up 2.50 markka at 333.50 -- after hitting 338.00 in early trade.
Forestries tracked a four percent rise in U.S. paper stocks overnight on news that James River and Fort Howard are merging, but the Helsinki forestry sub-index rose less, 1.14 percent.

Stromsdal rose the most -- almost five percent -- trailed by Metsa-Serla, Enso and UPM-Kymmene which all rose between one and three percent, and the sector was further supported by Portucel's announcement it believed there had been a sharp drop in Norscan pulp stocks in April.
Steel group Rautaruukki which traded for the first day with new shares rose 1.70 markka or over three percent to 49.00 markka in bumper volume.

Sporting goods and tobacco group Amer rose on its plans to abolish its unlisted but vote-strong K-shares, and analysts expected this to boost liquidity and international interest through the clearer ownership structure.
Orion was very strong -- up 5.90 markka at 202.00 -- after a 100,000-share in-house deal at Evli at 202.00. "There have been some very big buyers around," one broker said.
